title: Kant suppressed Swedenborg's disturbing accounts

tellings.quote: Kant admits that the reason that he did this is that the stuff in Swedenborg is so disturbing that it would destabilize society, including on a political level.

plain: The philosopher Jason Jorjani says that Immanuel Kant deliberately pushed aside the writings of Emanuel Swedenborg, an eighteenth-century Swedish mystic who described visits to spirits and other worlds. According to Jorjani, Kant "admits" he did it because the material in Swedenborg was "so disturbing that it would destabilize society, including on a political level." Jorjani tells this to Michels as a researcher, without pointing to the passage where Kant says so, and he credits Swedenborg's Arcana Coelestia (Secrets of Heaven), Kant's Groundwork of the Metaphysics of Morals and his own book Prometheus and Atlas.
